what_its_for: Loperamide is used to control and relieve diarrhea. It works by slowing down the movement of your gut, which allows your body to absorb more water and makes your stools less watery and less frequent. It can be used for sudden (acute) diarrhea or long-term (chronic) diarrhea in conditions like irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
how_to_take: Take loperamide by mouth with or without food. If you are using the liquid form, carefully measure your dose using the measuring cup or spoon that comes with the package — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. If you are using dissolving tablets (EZ Chews), let them dissolve on your tongue before swallowing. Drink plenty of fluids while you have diarrhea to stay hydrated. Do not take more than the recommended dose — taking too much can be very dangerous, including causing serious heart problems.
dosing: For adults and children 12 years and older: Start with 4 mg (two 2 mg capsules or tablets) after the first loose stool, then take 2 mg after each additional loose stool. Do not take more than 16 mg (eight 2 mg doses) in one day. For children 6 to 11 years: The dose is based on weight — always follow your doctor's instructions or the package label carefully. Do not give loperamide to children under 2 years old. Always follow your doctor's directions, as your dose may be different depending on your condition.
missed_dose: Loperamide is usually taken only when you have diarrhea, so a regular dosing schedule may not apply. If your doctor has told you to take it on a regular schedule and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store loperamide at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use loperamide after the expiration date printed on the package. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — check with your pharmacist about medicine take-back programs in your area.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking loperamide, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or drowsy after taking this medicine. Do not take loperamide if you have bloody diarrhea or diarrhea with a high fever, as this may be a sign of a serious infection. Do not take more than the recommended dose — misuse of loperamide, including taking high doses, can cause life-threatening heart rhythm problems. Avoid taking loperamide with certain medications like quinidine or ritonavir without talking to your doctor, as they can increase loperamide levels in your body to dangerous levels.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a fast, irregular, or pounding heartbeat; fainting or dizziness; severe stomach pain or bloating; constipation that does not go away; diarrhea that lasts more than 2 days (or 48 hours in children); blood or mucus in your stool; a high fever with your diarrhea; signs of severe dehydration such as dry mouth, little or no urination, dizziness, or extreme thirst. Also call your doctor before using loperamide if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have liver disease.
when_it_works: Loperamide usually starts to work within 1 to 3 hours after taking your first dose. Most people notice fewer and firmer stools within 24 to 48 hours. If your diarrhea does not improve after 2 days of using loperamide, stop taking it and contact your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using loperamide if you are pregnant. It should only be used if the benefit outweighs the risk. Breastfeeding: Small amounts of loperamide may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using it while breastfeeding. Children: Do not give loperamide to children under 2 years of age. Use with caution in young children and always follow the weight-based dosing on the label or your doctor's instructions. Older adults (65 and older): Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of loperamide, including constipation and dizziness. Liver disease: If you have liver problems, let your doctor know before taking loperamide, as it may build up in your body and cause harmful effects.
